name: Roast Chicken
summary: A plainly roasted chicken, basted often, after Fannie Farmer's 1896 method.
ingredients: 1 roasting chicken, 4 to 5 lb, cleaned and trussed
1 cup boiling water, for the pan
2 tbsp flour and 2 cups stock, for the gravy

equipment.help: The heat and the timing differ, so the steps after this follow the oven you pick.
equipment.label: Oven

steps.title: Wipe the bird
steps.body: Wipe the chicken inside and out with a damp cloth. Pat it dry.

steps.title: Season and flour
steps.body: Rub the bird all over with the softened butter, then sprinkle on the salt, pepper and flour.
steps.note: The flour is what browns the skin. Farmer called this dredging.

steps.title: Into the pan
steps.body: Lay the chicken breast up on a rack in the roasting pan. Pour the boiling water into the pan, not over the bird.

steps.title: Heat a gas oven to 400°F
steps.body: Gas ovens run hot at the top. Put the rack in the middle.

steps.title: Heat an electric oven to 400°F
steps.body: Wait for the preheat light before the bird goes in.

steps.title: Heat a convection oven to 375°F
steps.body: The fan does the work of a hotter oven, so drop the heat 25°F.

steps.title: Roast and baste
steps.body: Put the pan in the oven. Baste with the pan liquid every fifteen minutes.
steps.note: Basting is the whole trick. Set the timer again if you need longer.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: The leg joint should move freely and the juice from a deep cut should run clear, not pink.
steps.note: A thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh should read 165°F.

steps.title: Rest the bird
steps.body: Lift the chicken onto a warm platter and let it stand while you make the gravy.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.body: Pour off all but two tablespoons of fat. Stir in the flour, let it brown, then add the stock a little at a time and stir until it thickens.

steps.title: Carve and serve
steps.body: Carve at the table and pass the gravy separately.
